outcomes.text: Find the full subject and predicate in a simple statement.
Use a tree to distinguish a phrase’s category from its function.
Distinguish a modifier from a complement by checking its relation to a head.

opening.prompt: In “The boat near the pier is rocking”, which words identify what is rocking?

options.feedback: This leaves out the words identifying the boat.
The whole group identifies the boat.
These words locate the boat.

opening.prompt: In “The small bells rang twice”, which group says what happened?

options.feedback: This leaves out how often.
This names the subject.
These words give the action and how often it happened.

opening.prompt: In “Inez found the kite”, which group functions as the subject?

options.feedback: This is the group directly before the full predicate.
This group is inside the predicate.
This crosses the subject–predicate boundary.

opening.prompt: In “Rui carried a heavy parcel”, what can be left out to give “Rui carried a parcel”?

options.feedback: This removes the noun.
The description can be omitted.
The revised sentence still needs “a”.

opening.prompt: Which yes/no question keeps the tense and meaning of “The lid is rattling”?

options.feedback: That changes the tense.
This moves part of the predicate into the wrong position.
The auxiliary comes before the whole subject.

closing.prompt: In “The violin in its case was rattling”, where is the subject–predicate boundary?

options.feedback: The location words identify the violin and stay with the subject.
The question “Was the violin in its case rattling?” keeps that entire subject together.
“Was” belongs to the predicate in the statement.

closing.prompt: In “The visitor greeted the caretaker”, which NP is the subject, and why?

options.text: “The visitor”, because its NP is directly under S
options.feedback: The other NP is inside the VP.

options.text: “The caretaker”, because it names a person
options.feedback: Both NPs name people. Their positions distinguish the functions.
An NP’s category alone does not establish its function.

closing.prompt: In the V2 tree for “The shutters creaked”, which two nodes are sisters?

options.feedback: S is the parent of the subject NP.
S is the parent of the predicate VP.

options.text: The subject NP and the predicate VP
options.feedback: They share S as their immediate parent.

closing.prompt: In “Nico folded a damp towel”, which word modifies “towel”?

options.feedback: It adds a description. “Nico folded a towel” preserves the relation.
This noun is the head of the phrase.
This verb is in the larger predicate.

closing.prompt: In “Ava slipped beside the counter”, the whole location can be left out. Why does “the counter” still belong with “beside” in the original phrase?

options.text: Every part of an optional phrase is optional
options.feedback: Omitting a whole phrase tests a different relation from omitting one part inside it.

options.text: It supplies the landmark required by this use of “beside”
options.feedback: In this reading, the location is defined relative to the counter.
The landmark joins “beside” inside the location phrase.
